title: Decentralized Escalation Metadata Propagator for Traces & Alerts
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Build a lightweight metadata propagator that attaches a minimal, structured escalation payload to traces, logs, and alert events so downstream tools (PagerDuty, Slack, automated postmortem composer) can produce rich, actionable notifications without expensive trace rehydration. The propagator should run inside the tracing instrumentation layer and be pluggable across the runtime and sidecar collectors. Goals: 1) propagate a stable incident fingerprint, SLO bucket, suggested runbook URL, and short diagnostic hints (top-suspect-span-id, recent-error-count) with <1% latency overhead; 2) render consistent attachments in PD/Slack with trace snippets and quick-action buttons; 3) produce a seed for automated postmortem drafts when incidents are acknowledged/resolved.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing libraries emit 'escalation.metadata' with keys: fingerprint, slo_bucket, runbook_url, suspect_span, error_count; field sizes capped to 1024 bytes total.
PagerDuty webhook shows attachment with runbook link, fingerprint, and a 1-line trace snippet for >95% of test incidents.
Slack alert message includes 'Jump to span' link, runbook button, and a collapsed diagnostic section; UX validated by SRE and support reps.
End-to-end latency for instrumented requests increases by <1% p50 and <3% p99 in synthetic load tests.
Postmortem draft is auto-created in the incidents workspace with prefilled fingerprint and link to relevant traces for acknowledged incidents older than 5 minutes.
Documentation and migration guide published in Confluence with example instrumentation and PD rules.
implementation_notes: Propagator will be implemented as a small middleware component inside our tracing SDKs and as a Lua filter for OpenTelemetry collector to support Private deployments.
Metadata schema v1: fingerprint (sha1 hex), slo_bucket (string), runbook_url (url), suspect_span (trace/span id), error_count (int), sample_hint (low|medium|high).
Use dedicated opt-in header 'X-RD-ESC' for cross-service propagation; fallback to trace attributes for intra-process only flows.
To limit overhead, only set sample_hint=high for spans with error tags or latency > configured threshold; downstream collectors must respect sampling hints.

PagerDuty payloads will use Events API v2 with 'images' and 'links' fields populated; Slack messages rendered via message blocks and include action buttons that trigger ops-runbooks service endpoints.
Secret handling: runbook_url may contain internal IDs but not tokens; if runbook requires auth, button opens Console with SSO redirect.
Feature flag: feature.observe.escalation_propagator rollout by org for Hosted/Dedicated/Private with default off for existing customers.
Performance: instrumentation to be guarded with fast-path checks; add metrics: rd.escalation.emitted, rd.escalation.skipped_reason, rd.escalation.propagation_latency.
Compatibility: ensure headers obey max header size for common proxies; also provide compact base64 encoding option if needed.
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema validation, size caps, and header encoding/decoding.
Integration tests: end-to-end synthetic service mesh that triggers PD and Slack alerts and verifies attachments and links resolve to traces.
Load test: run synthetic traffic at 10k rps with 0.1% error rate to validate p99 impact and memory overhead.
Canary: enable for 5 internal teams for 72 hours, capture telemetry and runbook usage metrics.
Security review: ensure metadata cannot leak PII and that runbook_url does not expose secrets; engage SecOps prior to canary.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: SDK + collector implementation merged behind feature flag; internal QA and docs published.
Phase 2: Enable in Hosted for internal orgs (redwood-internal + 3 partner orgs) for 72-hour canary.
Phase 3: Gradual 10%->50%->100% rollout across accounts with monitoring windows at each step.
Phase 4: Add automatic postmortem seed creation for acknowledged incidents after 2 weeks of stable behavior.
monitoring_signals: Alert: escalation_emitted_drop_rate > 0.5% over 5m for canary orgs
Dashboard: Escalation Health - emission rate, avg metadata size, PD attachment success rate, Slack render errors
Log: structured errors when schema validation fails (include example payload truncated).
rollback_plan: Flip feature.observe.escalation_propagator off globally if emission_error_rate > 1% or p99 latency regression > 5% sustained for 10 minutes.
Revert PD/Slack attachment formatting via runtime templates (no code roll) if render errors spike.
Fast revert path documented and exercised during canary with runbook for ops engineers.
